lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the current broad Schizaeaceae through specialized fertile frond portions and a subapical annulus, then split project Anemia from Lygodium by erect modified fertile pinnae versus a climbing indeterminate rachis.

taxonomy_scope.project_teaching_treatment: Current Kew Schizaeaceae, including Anemia and Lygodium.
taxonomy_scope.historical_note: Flora of North America uses narrower Anemiaceae and Lygodiaceae concepts. Those older family names remain useful for morphology and search provenance but are not separate project families.

project_scope.selection_mode: Anemia mexicana + Lygodium japonicum project module
project_scope.note: Anemia mexicana is accepted and native from west-central Texas southward; Lygodium japonicum is accepted but introduced in Texas.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Find where the sporangia live. In this lineage the fertile portions of the frond are strongly specialized into contracted lobes, pinnae or sorophores rather than ordinary round/marginal sori on a normal blade.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Terrestrial ferns with highly variable fronds. Project Anemia is an ordinary ground fern; project Lygodium has an indeterminate twining rachis that acts like a vine.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Sporangia are borne singly or in rows on specialized fertile lobes/segments. The annulus is subapical and the sporangium opens by a longitudinal fissure.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Specialized fertile pinnae/lobes + subapical-annulus sporangia = current broad Schizaeaceae. Then ask whether the plant is an erect Anemia or climbing Lygodium.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: fertile-portion architecture → sporangium/annulus → Anemia fertile basal pinnae → Lygodium climbing rachis → Lygodium fertile fringe → Joey Pteridaceae contrast → family-name history
visual_lesson.intro: This family is memorable because the spore-bearing tissue is pushed into bizarre specialized parts. In Anemia a pair of basal pinnae becomes almost all sporangia; in Lygodium the frond keeps growing and climbs like a vine.

steps.title: 1 · Find the specialized fertile part
steps.look_for: Contracted fertile lobes or pinnae carrying rows of sporangia instead of ordinary sori on a broad blade.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the strongest visual break from the common fern families already in the learner.

steps.title: 2 · Show the subapical annulus
steps.look_for: The thickened annulus sits near the sporangium apex rather than forming the familiar vertical ring of many leptosporangiate ferns.
steps.why_it_matters: Explains why Schizaeales sporangia are structurally different from Pteridaceae/Polypodiaceae.

steps.title: 3 · Anemia mexicana door
steps.look_for: A 1-pinnate sterile blade with the proximal pair of pinnae transformed into tall narrow fertile structures, often rising above the rest of the blade.
steps.why_it_matters: FNA keys the Texas Anemia directly from this partially dimorphic 1-pinnate architecture.

steps.title: 4 · Put Anemia on limestone
steps.look_for: Fern rooted in lightly shaded limestone outcrop/crevice.
steps.why_it_matters: Anemia mexicana is a real Edwards Plateau dry-limestone fern, reinforcing that not all ferns are wet-shade plants.

steps.title: 5 · Lygodium door: the frond is the vine
steps.look_for: A long indeterminate rachis twining around surrounding vegetation, with repeated lateral pinnae.
steps.why_it_matters: This is one of the most unusual fern growth forms and an immediate genus-level cue.

steps.title: 6 · Find Lygodium fertile fringes
steps.look_for: Ultimate segments fringed with narrow fertile lobes/sorophores carrying sporangia.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirms a climbing fern rather than an ordinary vine.

steps.title: 7 · Compare with Joey's Adiantum
steps.look_for: Joey's Adiantum fertile frond shows spore-producing regions covered by a rolled leaflet margin (pseudoindusium), unlike Schizaeaceae's specialized contracted fertile structures.
steps.why_it_matters: Uses authoritative field footage to make the Schizaeaceae-vs-Pteridaceae reproductive split concrete.

steps.title: 8 · Learn the family-name history
steps.look_for: Older FNA: Anemiaceae + Lygodiaceae. Current Kew: both inside Schizaeaceae.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents apparently conflicting field guides and databases from creating duplicate families in the learner.

comparisons.title: Schizaeaceae vs Pteridaceae
comparisons.rule: Schizaeaceae puts sporangia on specialized contracted fertile lobes/pinnae and uses a subapical annulus. Local Pteridaceae commonly keeps sori on the ordinary blade margin under a rolled false indusium.

comparisons.title: Schizaeaceae vs Polypodiaceae
comparisons.rule: Pleopeltis has discrete round sori on an ordinary blade; Schizaeaceae shifts the sporangia onto visibly specialized fertile frond portions.

comparisons.title: Anemia vs Lygodium
comparisons.rule: Anemia mexicana is an erect terrestrial fern with a normal sterile blade and a specialized basal fertile pinna pair. Lygodium japonicum has a vine-like twining rachis and fertile lobes fringing pinnules.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not teach FNA's Anemiaceae/Lygodiaceae as additional current project families. They are valuable older morphological treatments, while the current canonical family backbone here follows Kew's broader Schizaeaceae.

genera.fast_cue: erect terrestrial fern + specialized proximal fertile pinnae + limestone Edwards Plateau habitat
